This page details '''statistics of the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup and UEFA Europa League]]'''. Unless notified these statistics concern all seasons since the inception of the UEFA Cup in the [[1971–72 UEFA Cup|1971–72 season]], including qualifying rounds.<ref>{{multiref2
|1={{cite web | url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/027c-16bb27585202-c2f661fa6a88-1000--europa-league-records-and-stats-clubs-players-matches-goals/ | title=Europa League records and stats: Clubs, players, matches, goals, wins | website=[[UEFA]] }}
|2={{cite web | url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0257-0e99f2c6eddb-e787f872f86f-1000--europa-league-group-stage-league-phase-records-and-stati/ | title=Europa League group stage/league phase records and statistics | website=[[UEFA]] }}
|3={{cite web | url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0251-0e987dba2198-4ca0099d9ed1-1000--europa-league-knockout-records-and-stats-clubs-players-mat/ | title=Europa League knockout records and stats: Clubs, players, matches, goals | website=[[UEFA]] }}
|4={{cite web | url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0252-0ce430367606-35094e8eef73-1000--europa-league-final-records-biggest-wins-oldest-scorers-/ | title=Europa League final records: Biggest wins, oldest scorers, youngest players, highest attendance | website=[[UEFA]] }}
}}</ref> The UEFA Cup replaced the [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] in the 1971–72 season, so the Fairs Cup is not considered a UEFA competition, and hence clubs' records in the Fairs Cup are not considered part of their European record.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/kind=1/newsid=2571.html|title=UEFA Cup: All-time finals|date=August 14, 2002|website=uefa.com - UEFA - News & Features - News Specific|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020814112952/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/kind=1/newsid=2571.html|archive-date=2002-08-14}}</ref>

==General performances==
===By club===
{{For|details on winning clubs|List of UEFA Cup and Europa League finals}}
A total of 31 clubs have won the tournament since its 1971 inception, with [[Sevilla F.C.|Sevilla]] being the only team to win it seven times, and only one to win three in a row. A total of fifteen clubs have won the tournament multiple times: the forementioned club, along with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], [[Inter Milan]], [[Atlético Madrid]], [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[IFK Göteborg]], [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]], [[Feyenoord]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[FC Porto|Porto]] and [[Eintracht Frankfurt]]. A total of 33 clubs have reached the final without ever managing to win the tournament.

Clubs from eleven countries have provided tournament winners. Spanish clubs have been the most successful, winning a total of fourteen titles. England is second with eleven, followed by Italy in third with ten, while the other multiple-time winners are Germany with seven, Netherlands with four, and Portugal, Sweden and Russia with two each. The only other countries to provide a tournament winner are Belgium, Ukraine, and Turkey. France, Scotland, Yugoslavia, Hungary, and Austria have all provided losing finalists.

The [[1979–80 UEFA Cup|1980 UEFA Cup]] saw four [[Bundesliga]] teams (i.e., [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], [[Eintracht Frankfurt]], [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], and [[VfB Stuttgart]]) make up all of the semi-finals competitors — a unique record for one country. Frankfurt beat Mönchengladbach in the final.

Clubs from a total of 56 European cities have participated in the tournament final. Clubs from 29 cities have provided winners, with the clear city leaders being [[Seville]] (seven), followed by [[London]] and [[Madrid]] (five each).

=== All-time points table ===
In this ranking, two points are awarded for a win, one for a draw, and zero for a loss. Following statistical convention in football, matches decided in extra time are counted as wins and losses, while matches decided by penalty shoot-outs are counted as draws. Teams are ranked by total points, then by goal difference, then by goals scored. Only the top twenty-five are listed (includes qualifying rounds).

==Undefeated champions==
* Nine teams have won the tournament undefeated in UEFA Cup history:
** [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] (1972)
** [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] (1979)
** [[IFK Göteborg|Göteborg]] (1982, 1987)
** [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] (1992)
** [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] (2000)
** [[Feyenoord]] (2002)
** [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] (2019)
** [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] (2021)
** [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] (2022)

==Consecutive wins==
* [[Atlético Madrid]] hold the record of most consecutive wins (both home and away) with 15 spanning the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League|2011–12]] and [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|2012–13]] seasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/479458-most-consecutive-wins-by-a-football-soccer-team-in-the-uefa-cup-europa-league |title=Most consecutive wins by a football (soccer) team in the UEFA Cup/Europa League |publisher=Guinness World Records |date=25 October 2012 }}</ref>

==Miscellaneous records==
* Only four clubs have won the treble of their national league championship, domestic cup competition and the UEFA Cup all in the same season:
** [[IFK Göteborg]] (1982)
** [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] (2000)
** [[FC Porto|Porto]] (2003, 2011)
** [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] (2005)

* In addition to the above, nine clubs (including IFK Göteborg again, and Liverpool doing so twice) won their national league championship and the UEFA Cup in the same season:
**[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] (1973, 1976)
** [[IFK Göteborg]] (1987)
** [[Feyenoord]] (1974)
** [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] (1975)
** [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] (1977)
** [[PSV Eindhoven]] (1978)
** [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (1986)
** [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] (2004)
** [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] (2008)

* During the [[1979–80 UEFA Cup|1979–80]] season, West Germany had five entrants including cup holders Borussia Mönchengladbach. All five managed to reach the quarter-final stage and both semi-finals ended up being all-West German affairs. Ultimately, Eintracht Frankfurt defeated Borussia Mönchengladbach in the final. No West German club that season was eliminated by a non-German club.
* During the [[1997–98 UEFA Cup|1997–98]] season, France had seven entrants: [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]] as winner of the Coupe de la Ligue, [[FC Nantes|Nantes]], [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] and [[FC Metz|Metz]] as third, fourth and fifth placed respectively in Division 1, and also [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]], [[SC Bastia|Bastia]] and [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] as [[1997 UEFA Intertoto Cup]] Group winners. Nevertheless, only Auxerre reached the quarter-finals, where they were eliminated by [[SS Lazio|Lazio]].
* [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] are the only club to win the UEFA Cup/Europa League three times consecutively, in [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League|2014]], [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League|2015]] and [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|2016]]. [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] were the first club to win two in a row in [[1984–85 UEFA Cup|1985]] and [[1985–86 UEFA Cup|1986]], matched by Sevilla in [[2005–06 UEFA Cup|2006]] and [[2006–07 UEFA Cup|2007]].
* Only two countries have provided the champion in three consecutive seasons:
** Italy: between [[1988–89 UEFA Cup|1988–89]] and [[1990–91 UEFA Cup|1990–91]] ([[SSC Napoli|Napoli]], [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and [[Inter Milan]] the winners) and between [[1992–93 UEFA Cup|1992–93]] and [[1994–95 UEFA Cup|1994–95]] (Juventus, Inter Milan and [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]]).
** Spain: 2014, 2015 and 2016 (all Sevilla).

* Several times, winning the UEFA Cup was a club's only chance to qualify for European competition in the next season. A win by such a mid-table (and non-domestic-cup-winning) club then led to an extra place in the UEFA Cup (or an extra place in the [[UEFA Champions League]] since 2015) for the country in question. ==Individuals' goals==
===Most goals in a single match===
{{see also|List of UEFA Europa League hat-tricks}}
The record for most goals scored in a single match across all UEFA Cup/Europa League seasons is held by [[Eldar Hadžimehmedović]], after he scored six goals for [[Lyn Fotball|Lyn]] against [[NSÍ Runavík]] in the [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|2003–04]] qualifying round.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lyn 6–0 NSI Runavik|url=https://www.whoscored.com/Matches/57645/Live/Europe-UEFA-Europa-League-2003-2004-Lyn-NSI-Runavik|work=WhoScored|access-date=11 October 2018|date=11 October 2018}}</ref>

==Scorelines==
* Highest win in one leg, most goals in game:
** [[1984–85 UEFA Cup|1984–85]], First round:
*** [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] 14–0 [[FA Red Boys Differdange|Red Boys Differdange]]
* Highest aggregate win, most goals in tie:
** [[1972–73 UEFA Cup|1972–73]], First round:
*** [[Feyenoord]] 9–0 [[US Rumelange|Rumelange]]
*** [[US Rumelange|Rumelange]] 0–12 [[Feyenoord]]
*** Feyenoord won 21–0 on aggregate
* Best second-leg comebacks: (4 goals)
** [[1984–85 UEFA Cup|1984–85]], Second round:
*** [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] 6–2 [[FK Partizan|Partizan]]
*** [[FK Partizan|Partizan]] 4–0 [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]]
*** 6–6 on aggregate, Partizan won on away goals
**[[1985–86 UEFA Cup|1985–86]], Third round:
*** [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] 5–1 [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]
*** [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] 4–0 [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]]
*** 5–5 on aggregate, Real Madrid won on away goals
** [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League|2018–19]], Third qualifying round:
*** [[FC Dinamo Minsk|Dinamo Minsk]] 4–0 [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]]
*** [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] 8–1 [[FC Dinamo Minsk|Dinamo Minsk]] {{aet}} (4–0 after 90 minutes)
*** Zenit Saint Petersburg won 8–5 on aggregate
* Best away-leg come-back after losing home leg: (3 goals)
** [[2009–10 UEFA Europa League|2009–10]], play-off round:
*** [[FC Dinamo București|Dinamo București]] 0–3 [[FC Slovan Liberec|Slovan Liberec]]
*** [[FC Slovan Liberec|Slovan Liberec]] 0–3 [[FC Dinamo București|Dinamo București]] {{aet}}
*** Dinamo București won 9–8 on penalties
* Final comeback:
** [[1988 UEFA Cup Final|1988]]:
*** [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] 3–0 [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]]
*** [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] 3–0 [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] {{aet}}  
*** 3–3 on aggregate, Bayer Leverkusen won 3–2 on penalties
* Highest aggregate score in the final:
** [[1993 UEFA Cup Final|1993]]:
*** [[Borussia Dortmund]] 1–3 [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]
*** [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] 3–0 [[Borussia Dortmund]]
*** Juventus won 6–1 on aggregate
